subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Mechanical Advantage: Getting More From Less
description: A quick, practical guide to Mechanical Advantage: Getting More From Less.

hook.text: A machine with mechanical advantage of 5 turns 10 newtons of effort into 50 newtons of output.

buildup.text: Mechanical advantage is output force divided by input force. Higher means you push less to lift more.

discovery.text: Every simple machine trades distance for force. The total work stays the same — energy is conserved.

twist.text: Friction steals some energy as heat. Real mechanical advantage is always less than the ideal number.

climax.text: Engineers pick machines that match the job. High force? Use pulleys. High speed? Use levers.

punchline.text: Machines don't create force. They redirect it.

quiz.question: Why is real mechanical advantage always less than ideal?
options: Because machines naturally generate extra force over time
Because friction converts some input energy into heat
Because output distance is always greater than input distance
